checks.name: actual_project_doctor_and_repair
checks.result: The real P5-003 development session was inspected at revision 209. Doctor detected a real ledger progress edit without changing the cached next action, source bytes or project revision. After explicit reindex to 211, all 7 sources and 2 artifacts passed. A complete 4976-token L1 context supplied the saved checkpoint hash. Explicit interrupt-session repair closed that selected development session and its claim at revision 214, preserved its checkpoint and source bytes, and produced a session-scoped receipt. A fresh Doctor result had no findings.

checks.name: bounded_code_review
checks.result: A separate read-only reviewer checked Runtime/CLI read-only behavior, source identity/config parity, artifact path/hash checks, selected-repair response scope and FK-failure handling. The primary agent reviewed Store changes and required receipt scope plus historical-claim/parent-branch corrections; those corrections have targeted regressions. This is feature-local code review, not independent E4 business acceptance.

limitations: Feature-local validation and actual project self-use, not E4 scenario completion, a system benchmark or release. Process liveness is not inferred from active status or age. Pending saves/imports may still be in flight; no automatic interruption, artifact deletion, source rewrite, mutation application, database reconstruction or branch merge is attempted. Repair success applies only to the selected object; remaining findings require a fresh Doctor run. SQLite corruption/schema/FK failures block repair; readable current-schema FK failures still permit named read-only diagnostics. Source reads and artifact hashing are bounded and never emit content.
